narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Abraham; steady and grave.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking to Abraham and others; majestic, calm, sovereign.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.note: The patriarch (Abram until 17:5), near a hundred years old; reverent, hospitable, bold yet humble in pleading.

abimelech.name: Abimelech
abimelech.note: King of Gerara; protests his innocence to God, indignant with Abraham, then generous.

1.t: Abraham removed from thence to the south country, and dwelt between Cades and Sur, and sojourned in Gerara.

2.t: And he said of Sara his wife:
So Abimelech the king of Gerara sent, and took her.

3.t: And God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and he said to him:
Lo thou shalt die for the woman that thou hast taken: for she hath a husband.

4.t: Now Abimelech had not touched her, and he said:
Lord, wilt thou slay a nation that is ignorant and just?

5.t: Did not he say to me: She is my sister: and she say, He is my brother? in the simplicity of my heart, and cleanness of my hands have I done this.

6.t: And I know that thou didst it with a sincere heart: and therefore I withheld thee from sinning against me, and I suffered thee not to touch her.

7.t: Now therefore restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet: and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: but if thou wilt not restore her, know that thou shalt surely die, thou and all that are thine.

8.t: And Abimelech forthwith rising up in the night, called all his servants: and spoke all these words in their hearing, and all the men were exceedingly afraid.

9.t: And Abimelech called also for Abraham, and said to him:
What hast thou done to us? what have we offended thee in, that thou hast brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done to us what thou oughtest not to do.

10.t: And again he expostulated with him, and said:
What sawest thou, that thou hast done this?

11.t: I thought with myself, saying: Perhaps there is not the fear of God in this place: and they will kill me for the sake of my wife:

12.t: Howbeit, otherwise also she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father, and not the daughter of my mother, and I took her to wife.

13.t: And after God brought me out of my father's house, I said to her: Thou shalt do me this kindness: In every place, to which we shall come, thou shalt say that I am thy brother.

14.t: And Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and gave to Abraham: and restored to him Sara his wife,

15.t: The land is before you, dwell wheresoever it shall please thee.

16.t: Behold I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver, this shall serve thee for a covering of thy eyes to all that are with thee, and whithersoever thou shalt go: and remember thou wast taken.

17.t: And when Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech and his wife, and his handmaids, and they bore children:

18.t: For the Lord had closed up every womb of the house of Abimelech, on account of Sara, Abraham's wife.
